title: AstroForge is putting AI in command of its next spacecraft
slides: AstroForge's next spacecraft: can AI fly it safely?
The asteroid-mining startup will let AI navigate and make decisions.
But AI's decisions will go through 10-second human veto window.
This shift means mission control must trust algorithms in real time.
If you work in ops, start rehearsing human-AI handoffs now.
thread_text:
1. AI flies, humans veto

AstroForge's next asteroid-mining spacecraft will let AI navigate and make decisions, but every call goes through a 10-second human veto window.

2. The 10-second gap

That window is the entire safety net. If the AI makes a wrong move, mission control has ten seconds to catch it and override.

3. Trust in real time

Operators must now trust algorithms live, not after the fact. The shift turns mission control into a human-AI handoff team.

4. Training gap

Most ops teams have never rehearsed a 10-second veto. The asteroid-mining startup is betting they can learn fast enough.

5. Rehearse the handoff

Run a drill today: give a teammate a 10-second window to veto a simulated AI decision. If you haven't done it, start there.

instagram.caption:
Ten seconds. That's the entire safety net between an AI decision and a wrong move in space.

AstroForge's next asteroid-mining spacecraft will let AI navigate and call the shots, with mission control holding a 10-second veto window on every decision. 🚀

That means operators now trust algorithms live, not after the fact — and most ops teams have never rehearsed a handoff that fast.

If you run a control room, your job just became real-time algorithm supervision. 🧠

Run the drill today: hand a teammate a simulated AI call and give them 10 seconds to veto it. ⏱️

If you miss the window, who catches it?
